newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOCUS - Finland to offer Kemira shares.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Finland to offer Kemira shares.

text.p: Chemicals group Kemira announced plans to issue new shares, despite making a recent profits warning, while the Finish government also said on Tuesday it would sell of some of its stake in the firm.
Kemira Oy said it planned to seek permission to issue up to eight million new shares -- which would boost its current share capital of 1.21 billion markka ($266.6 million) by about seven percent.

The government, which had already flagged its aim of selling more Kemira stock, said on Tuesday it planned to lower its stake to 55 percent from 72.3 percent now. It has authority to lower its stake in the company to 50.1 percent.
Kemira's performance has improved steadily throughout the 1990s, even though it warned last month that weak pigments markets would pressure this year's operating earnings.

But analysts looking to a recovery in Europe see substantial profit growth for Kemira in prospect, and with the Helsinki bourse generally buoyant they said the extra share supply may be better received if it comes sooner rather than later.
"I would be good if they would do it soon," said Mats Lindholm at Carnegie Securities.
Kemira also said it would bring forward the publication of its January-August report to October 3, which analysts noted may hint at the offering's timing.

The only shadow Lindholm could see over an offering was the weak titanium oxide market -- but Kemira has said any weakness in operating profits should be more than offset at the net level by falling financial costs.

Most analysts declined to make any public comment on prospects for the offering, in the hope of playing some role in it, but agreed the market situation should be favourable enough to absorb the extra supply of shares.

They analysts were vague on the question of pricing, noting Kemira has retreated from a peak of 53.00 markka after the government in July appointed an adviser on the question of broadening Kemira's ownership.

Kemira's stock fell 1.50 markka or three percent to 47.50 after the announcement, putting its performance so far this year at 25 percent. With the Helsinki general index up 21 percent on the year so far, Kemira remains a mild outperformer.
One analyst said that because the share price had pulled back this suggested that the shares would be offered at a narrow discount, at best.

Consensus forecasts from 16 analysts for Kemira's 1996 and 1997 earnings per share collected by Edinburgh Financial Publishing (EFP) put it at six markka in 1996, up 30 percent from 4.6 markka in 1995, and at 6.70 in 1997.
The consensus forecasts put Kemira now at a prospective price-earnings ratio of eight times 1996 earnings, and seven times 1997 -- against around 12 times for the Helsinki bourse.
European chemicals companies currently trade around 11 times 1996 earnings and nine times 1997 earnings, analysts said, so on that basis Kemira would already look cheap.
"Kemira could return to the 53 peak once the issue and 1996 results are out of the way," said one Helsinki analyst requesting anonymity.

A final decision on the state offering will be subject to market conditions at the appropriate time, the trade and industry ministry said. Kemira will hold an extraordinary shareholders' meeting on September 25.
